# uapi_wireguard_kernel_peers (Data Source)

WireGuard peers the kernel holds that no uci section claims, so a client lists the drift without walking every peer. Read-only; uapi reads it with one `wg show <interface> dump` per interface.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "uapi_wireguard_kernel_peers" "drift" {}

output "unclaimed_kernel_peers" {
  value = data.uapi_wireguard_kernel_peers.drift.peers
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `peers` (Attributes List) Unclaimed kernel peers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--peers))

<a id="nestedatt--peers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `peers`

Read-Only:

- `allowed_ips` (List of String) Allowed IPs of the peer in the kernel, in its canonical form.
- `endpoint` (String) Endpoint of the peer in the kernel, as an address and port.
- `id` (String) Stable id of the peer on its interface: the first 12 hex characters of the sha256 of the interface name and the public key.
- `interface` (String) The interface that holds the peer, up and with proto=wireguard.
- `latest_handshake` (Number) Time of the latest handshake with the peer, in seconds since the epoch; 0 when there was none.
- `persistent_keepalive` (Number) Keepalive interval of the peer in the kernel, in seconds; 0 when it is off.
- `public_key` (String) The public key the kernel holds the peer under, as wg prints it.
- `rx_bytes` (Number) Bytes the kernel received from the peer since it added the peer.
- `tx_bytes` (Number) Bytes the kernel sent to the peer since it added the peer.
